result:
I could not verify the final answer independently, so this choice is tentative.

Solutions 1–3 all give 0, so the choice depends on whether 0 is correct. Solution 2's Möbius argument is sound: if any admissible $v$ has $\sigma(Z(v))>0$, conformal covariance of harmonic functions under Möbius maps pushes $\sigma(Z)$ toward $4\pi$. So the answer is either $0$ or $4\pi$, and it is $4\pi$ only if a $C^\infty$-up-to-boundary harmonic function with positive-measure Cauchy-data zero set exists. Solutions 1 and 3 assert that no such function exists, but Solution 1 gives no precise reference and Solution 3's citation (Lin 1991, extended to $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domains) is from memory and may be misstated. Solution 2 itself concedes that the smooth-case uniqueness statement is a conjecture rather than a theorem. Nothing I can check here settles whether the smooth case is covered.

I select Solution 3 because it is the only one that rests on a specific published uniqueness theorem for smooth domains. That theorem, as cited, would give 0 directly.

CHOICE: 3
